Dear Shankar,
You asked what it was like to go to the gurdwara with Jasmeet's family for her grandfather's anniversary. I want to tell you properly, because I nearly got it wrong.
When the kirtan began, the whole hall started singing together, slowly, eyes half closed. I didn't know the words. I wasn't sure if I, a guest from a Muslim family, should sing along or stay quiet. So I covered my head like everyone, sat on the floor at the back, and watched. Some aunties were smiling, some had tears. I couldn't tell if it was grief for her grandfather or joy in the singing, maybe both.
After a while Jasmeet's mother leaned over and whispered that I was welcome to join the refrain. So I did, softly. I felt calmer than I had in weeks.
With love,
Salma
